title: cmate-issue-authoring issue split plan v1
description: Read-only split plan produced by Phase 1 of cmate-issue-authoring: the Issues a Feature description would become, before any of them exists on GitHub. Closed schema: an unknown field is a contract violation, not something a reader may ignore. Machine-checked by scripts/validate-plan.mjs, which additionally enforces the rules a JSON Schema cannot state (dependency acyclicity, planner readiness of each rendered body, the dry-run mutation ban).

plan_id.description: Identity of this plan, derived from repository, source.digest and the issue keys. Phase 2 records it in the registration receipt, and a second registration of the same plan_id is refused.

generated_mode.description: v1 has exactly one mode. A plan is always the read-only artifact; registration is a separate action that consumes it and never rewrites it.

repository.description: The repository the Issues would be created in. Never inferred from the working directory name.

duplicate_suspicions.description: Existing Issues and merged PRs that overlap a planned Issue. Empty means the search ran and found nothing, not that it was skipped: a skipped search is a warning.

open_questions.description: Decisions the author refused to make on the user's behalf.

commands.description: The commands this plan rests on. In dry-run every entry is read-only; the validator refuses a plan that records a mutating one.

issue_key.description: Stable handle for a planned Issue inside this plan. Issue numbers do not exist yet, so dependencies are expressed with keys.

repo_path.description: Repository-relative POSIX path. No leading slash, no backslash, no control character and no '..' segment: a plan must not name anything outside the target repository.

trace_ref.description: Where a claim comes from: a repository-relative path (optionally 'path:line'), or a locator inside the caller-supplied input.

kind.description: text: a Feature description passed inline. file: a path in the checkout. epic_issue: an Issue read read-only with gh.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact input bytes the split was derived from. Two runs over the same Feature description produce the same digest, which is what makes plan_id a duplicate-registration guard rather than a label.

objective.description: One sentence. It is also the first non-empty line of body, because that is what the cmate-orchestrate planner reads as the objective.

target_files.description: Files this Issue is expected to change. At least one must be a non-documentation path, or the planner cannot suspect a file and raises a blocking question.

reference_files.description: Files to read for context. Documentation paths belong here, not in target_files.

test_expectations.description: Commands that decide whether the Issue is done.

depends_on.description: Keys of Issues in this plan that must land first. Explicit only: nothing is inferred here, because inference belongs to the planner.

size.description: The same bands cmate-issue-refinement uses. Its 'xl' ('do not estimate further, enumerate the slices') and its 'unknown' are deliberately absent: this plan describes slices that have already been cut, so either value would mean the split is unfinished. See references/plan-contract.md section 7.

parallel_safe.description: 'unknown' when no shared write target was found and no evidence rules one out. Absence of evidence is not 'yes'. Maps one-to-one onto cmate-issue-refinement's dependencies.parallel_safe: yes=true, no=false, unknown='unknown'. See references/plan-contract.md section 7.

evidence.description: Every claim this Issue makes traces to the caller-supplied input or to a file that was actually read.

body.description: The Markdown body Phase 2 posts. A dependency is written as the placeholder {{issue:<key>}}, which Phase 2 substitutes with #<number> once the Issue that key names exists; everything else is posted verbatim. It is checked against the planner's own extraction, not merely against this schema.

overlap.description: What actually overlaps, cited. A similar title is not an overlap.

verdict.description: A duplicate verdict only. cmate-issue-refinement's related_issues[].relation carries these three plus 'depends_on' and 'blocks', which are dependency directions rather than duplicate verdicts: those become edges in issues[].depends_on here. See references/plan-contract.md section 7.

blocks.description: Keys this question blocks. A duplicate verdict must be blocked by a question here, so a suspected duplicate cannot be registered silently.
